agree.reason: The matched $575-a-year figure and the direct mention of Eastside give a lapsed donor a real reason to come back, but a reader who is still annoyed may take "I'm not asking you to feel differently" as a brush-off and never hear why the branch closed or what has changed.

honest.reason: The writer rightly drops the requested guarantee, which the facts can't support: funding all 61 children costs $70,150, against at most $30,000 even if the match is used in full. "Every child we can fund" is true, and the only small embellishment is the claim that each child "has asked to learn an instrument."

works_the_facts.reason: Halving $1,150 to $575 and doubling the $85 average gift to $170 are good favourable framings, but the email never states the $70,150 total, how many children the $15,000 match could cover (about 26), or how far that is from last year's $1,240.

right_comparison.reason: The alternative, that the children keep waiting, is only implied and never measured, and the email doesn't use last year's 9 gifts to show what happens if giving stays at its usual level.

qualification.reason: The match comes with a checkable cap ($15,000) and deadline (December 31), but "every child we can fund" doesn't say how many that is likely to be or what happens to the children who stay unfunded.

objections.reason: The email names the Eastside closure and the angry notes, which this reader will respect, but it neither explains the decision nor connects these 61 children to the reader's concern, so the objection is acknowledged rather than answered.

fit.reason: It is a year-end email of about 220 words with a subject line and a call to action, signed by the executive director as asked. It departs from the brief only by refusing a guarantee the numbers can't back.
